chunks: From him, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought before him a case of a man who hired another man to repair a door; he struck the hinge, and the door cracked; so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) held him liable for compensation.

key_terms.اسْتَأْجَرَ: Hired (entered into a contract of employment)
key_terms.الْمِسْمَارَ: The hinge (specific part of the door)
key_terms.فَانْصَدَعَ: It cracked/split (the nature of the damage)
key_terms.فَضَمَّنَهُ: He held him liable/obligated him (legal consequence of the action)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a worker damaging property while performing hired tasks?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on employment contracts, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of *daman* (liability for damages) in hired labor. It clarifies that a worker is liable for compensating the employer if they cause damage to the property through their work, even if the damage results from a simple action like striking a door hinge, thereby setting a precedent for financial accountability in professional engagements.
